buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE: The Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity to be ordered up to 25 percent of bid quantity at the time of placement of contract. The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. Scope of Supply Scope of supply (Bid price to include all cost components) : Only supply of Goods 3. Certificates ISO 9001: The bidder or the OEM of the offered products must have ISO 9001 certification. 4. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 5. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Additional terms and conditions 1. The approved Vendor will supply the items immediately or latest within 15 days of placing of purchase or der. 2. If the approved Vendor fails to execute the purchase order within the stipulated period of 15 days, a pena lty of 0.5 percent of the value of the order calculated at the contract rate per week or a part of a week will be levied. The maximum penalty for late supply shall not exceed 10% of the total value of the order/orders . An approved Vendor can seek extension of the delivery period with the prior consent of the Competent A uthority, if it is not in a position to execute the order in time. The extension of delivery period cannot be cl aimed as a matter of right but will be at the discretion of Competent Authority.

3. it is incumbent upon the approved Vendor to supply the item as per the specifications and quantity menti oned in the purchase order. 4. If the items/ drugs are not supplied by the Vendor within six weeks of the purchase order in full or in part, the order in respect of the quantity not supplied is liable to be cancelled at the risk and expense of approv ed Vendor. 5. The purchaser will not pay separately for transit insurance and the approved Vendor will be responsible f or delivery of items covered by the supply order in good condition at the specified destination and for this purpose freight, insurance, Octroi etc, if any, will have to be borne by the Vendor. The consignee will, as so on as possible, but not later than 30 days of the date of arrival of stores at destination, notify the contracto r of any loss or damage to the stores, that may have occurred during the transit. 6. During transit, approved Vendor should maintain the recommended temperature of the drug (wherever in dicated), otherwise if on checking it is found that temperature has not been maintained, supply against the said order is liable to be rejected and cancelled. It will be counted as a non-supply. 7. The prices approved are FOR destination per unit and are exclusive of GST except where indicated but inc lusive of all charges for packing and forwarding. 8. The approved Vendor will have to supply drugs directly in the quantity ordered, to ESIC Medical College a nd Hospital, Gulbarga. The approved Vendor shall not, at any time, assign, sub-let or make over the contra ct or the benefit thereof or any part thereof to any person or persons. In case, at any stage of the contract, it is found that the approved Vendor has appointed the distributors/dealers/third party agent for making su pply or receiving of supply order against the contract, ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Gulbarga will initi ate the following actions against the approved Vendor(s): a. 100% forfeiture of Performance Security b. Blacklisting for participation in the future tender enquiries for ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Gulbar ga for a period of two years prospectively. 9. Each packing shall be printed with nomenclature of the drug and shall be labelled in accordance with the requirement of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the rules made there under. Packing & packaging o f each drug must comply with the procedure provided under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 and rules made there under. 10. Packing a. Loose supplies/damaged packing/tempered or damaged labeled supplies shall not be accepte d under any circumstances. b. Supplies to be made in proper boxes. c. Liquid orals to be supplied only in glass/ plastic bottles conforming to Drugs & Cosmetics Act and rules made there under. d. Large volume parenterals to be supplied only in plastic bottles / polypacks conforming to Dru gs & Cosmetics Act and rules made there under. e. It should be ensured that only first use packaging material of uniform size including Bottles a

nd vials should be used for making supplies. f. All primary packing containers should be strictly conforming to the specifications described/ mentioned in the relevant pharmacopoeia. g. Packing should be able to prevent damage or deterioration during transit. h. All containers i.e. bottle, tins, cartons, tubes etc., are required to be secured with pilfer-proof seals to ensure genuineness of the products packed and the correctness of the contents. MRP should not be written on any labels otherwise it will be disqualified. 11. Each consignment shall be accompanied by the applicable invoice, delivery challan, batchwise details and expiry details and other documents required under the contract and applicable regulations. 12. Life Period a. For Drugs having shelf life of Two years or less: As on the date of delivery, Drugs should not b e older than one fourth (1/4) of its shelf life from the date of manufacture. b. For Drugs having shelf life more than Two years: As on the date of delivery, Drugs should not be older than one sixth (1/6) of its shelf life from the date of manufacture. c. Imported Drugs: As on the date of delivery, Drugs should have a minimum 50% of valid shelf l ife from the date of manufacture. d. Notwithstanding the above, the Competent Authority/Authorized nominated officer by Compe tent Authority may relax this criteria in case of exigencies with reasons duly recorded and shall be responsible for use of that stores within its given shelf life, with a suitable undertaking from the supplier, the terms of which shall be decided by the consignee as per the requirement of t he stores and usage pattern. The Consignee should ensure that there should not be any financ ial loss to the ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Gulbarga. 13. Pharmacopoeia Specification IP/BP/USP etc. should be clearly mentioned against each drug/constituent of the formulation supplied as per the provisions of Drug and Cosmetics Act. 14. The items accepted should comply with the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder as amended upto date and Drug Price Control Order. 15. It should be ensured that ISI Code No. is indicated on the packing and at the time of supplies, it must be e nsured that the items supplied has ISI Mark as well as Code No.,as is the statutory requirement of the Bure au of Indian Standards (Where ever Applicable). 16. Testing of Drugs – Quality Control a. Approved Vendor should mandatorily submit a Test Report for that particular batch of medici nes tested by the Government/Government approved Laboratories along with each supply, failing which supply received will be liable for rejection at the inspection stage and penalty of l ate supply will be levied as per provisions. b. The Competent Authority shall be at liberty to undertake regular and random testing of the dr ugs supplied by the approved Vendors at regular interval to maintain and ensure the quality of drugs. c. Details of the items found not of standard quality should be brought to the notice of the Comp etent Authority along with the test reports immediately. A copy of the test report should be se

nt immediately to the firm, the concerned Drug controllers, and respective Central Drug Contro l authorities for necessary action. d. The report of the Govt./Govt. approved laboratory shall be accepted by the approved Vendor. In case the same is disputed by the approved Vendor the report of the Appellate Laboratory on ly will be accepted as final. However, the same should be submitted within three months, from the date of communication of the disputed test report to the approved Pharmaceutical firm. Fo r this, the approved Vendor should approach the concerned Drug Control Authorities for gettin g the drugs tested, as per procedure, from the Appellate Laboratory at their own cost. In case no response is received from the approved Vendor within the stipulated period, action as dee med fit as per terms & conditions of the contract will be initiated. e. For imported items: - The approved Vendor must submit the In-house test report of Principal manufacturer with each and every batch of supply. f. If any drug/s supplied against this contract are found to be "Not of Standard Quality" on inspe ction by Competent Authority, the approved Vendor will be liable to replace the entire quantity within 15 days otherwise risk purchase will be charged from the approved Vendor. g. If the product is found to be "Not of Standard Quality", the cost of testing will be recovered fro m the approved Vendor. 17. If any item/Batch of the item declared Not of Standard quality (NSQ), action may be taken against the ven dor including Recall of the NSQ item from ESIC Medical College and Hospital Gulbarga and Suitable forfeitu re of Performance Security. 18. Earnest Money Deposit (EMD): Bidders participating in the Antibiotic, Antiviral, and Antif ungal Group shall mandatorily submit an Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) of ₹40,044/- (Rupees F orty Thousand and Forty-Four Only) in the favour of Medical Superintendent , ESICMCH, Kalab uragi. 19. Earnest Money Deposit (EMD): Bidders participating in the anaesthetics Group shall manda torily submit an Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) of ₹24,453/- (Rupees Twenty Four thousand F our hundred Fifty three Only) in the favour of Medical Superintendent, ESICMCH, Kalaburagi; 20. Bidders who are exempted from paying EMD must mandatorily submit the Bid Securing Declaration form as the format given:

1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE: The Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity to be ordered up to 25 percent of bid quantity at the time of placement of contract. The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. Scope of Supply Scope of supply (Bid price to include all cost components) : Only supply of Goods 3. Certificates ISO 9001: The bidder or the OEM of the offered products must have ISO 9001 certification. 4. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 5. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Additional terms and conditions 1. The approved Vendor will supply the items immediately or latest within 15 days of placing of purchase or der. 2. If the approved Vendor fails to execute the purchase order within the stipulated period of 15 days, a pena lty of 0.5 percent of the value of the order calculated at the contract rate per week or a part of a week will be levied. The maximum penalty for late supply shall not exceed 10% of the total value of the order/orders . An approved Vendor can seek extension of the delivery period with the prior consent of the Competent A uthority, if it is not in a position to execute the order in time. The extension of delivery period cannot be cl aimed as a matter of right but will be at the discretion of Competent Authority.

3. it is incumbent upon the approved Vendor to supply the item as per the specifications and quantity menti oned in the purchase order. 4. If the items/ drugs are not supplied by the Vendor within six weeks of the purchase order in full or in part, the order in respect of the quantity not supplied is liable to be cancelled at the risk and expense of approv ed Vendor. 5. The purchaser will not pay separately for transit insurance and the approved Vendor will be responsible f or delivery of items covered by the supply order in good condition at the specified destination and for this purpose freight, insurance, Octroi etc, if any, will have to be borne by the Vendor. The consignee will, as so on as possible, but not later than 30 days of the date of arrival of stores at destination, notify the contracto r of any loss or damage to the stores, that may have occurred during the transit. 6. During transit, approved Vendor should maintain the recommended temperature of the drug (wherever in dicated), otherwise if on checking it is found that temperature has not been maintained, supply against the said order is liable to be rejected and cancelled. It will be counted as a non-supply. 7. The prices approved are FOR destination per unit and are exclusive of GST except where indicated but inc lusive of all charges for packing and forwarding. 8. The approved Vendor will have to supply drugs directly in the quantity ordered, to ESIC Medical College a nd Hospital, Gulbarga. The approved Vendor shall not, at any time, assign, sub-let or make over the contra ct or the benefit thereof or any part thereof to any person or persons. In case, at any stage of the contract, it is found that the approved Vendor has appointed the distributors/dealers/third party agent for making su pply or receiving of supply order against the contract, ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Gulbarga will initi ate the following actions against the approved Vendor(s): a. 100% forfeiture of Performance Security b. Blacklisting for participation in the future tender enquiries for ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Gulbar ga for a period of two years prospectively. 9. Each packing shall be printed with nomenclature of the drug and shall be labelled in accordance with the requirement of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the rules made there under. Packing & packaging o f each drug must comply with the procedure provided under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 and rules made there under. 10. Packing a. Loose supplies/damaged packing/tempered or damaged labeled supplies shall not be accepte d under any circumstances. b. Supplies to be made in proper boxes. c. Liquid orals to be supplied only in glass/ plastic bottles conforming to Drugs & Cosmetics Act and rules made there under. d. Large volume parenterals to be supplied only in plastic bottles / polypacks conforming to Dru gs & Cosmetics Act and rules made there under. e. It should be ensured that only first use packaging material of uniform size including Bottles a

nd vials should be used for making supplies. f. All primary packing containers should be strictly conforming to the specifications described/ mentioned in the relevant pharmacopoeia. g. Packing should be able to prevent damage or deterioration during transit. h. All containers i.e. bottle, tins, cartons, tubes etc., are required to be secured with pilfer-proof seals to ensure genuineness of the products packed and the correctness of the contents. MRP should not be written on any labels otherwise it will be disqualified. 11. Each consignment shall be accompanied by the applicable invoice, delivery challan, batchwise details and expiry details and other documents required under the contract and applicable regulations. 12. Life Period a. For Drugs having shelf life of Two years or less: As on the date of delivery, Drugs should not b e older than one fourth (1/4) of its shelf life from the date of manufacture. b. For Drugs having shelf life more than Two years: As on the date of delivery, Drugs should not be older than one sixth (1/6) of its shelf life from the date of manufacture. c. Imported Drugs: As on the date of delivery, Drugs should have a minimum 50% of valid shelf l ife from the date of manufacture. d. Notwithstanding the above, the Competent Authority/Authorized nominated officer by Compe tent Authority may relax this criteria in case of exigencies with reasons duly recorded and shall be responsible for use of that stores within its given shelf life, with a suitable undertaking from the supplier, the terms of which shall be decided by the consignee as per the requirement of t he stores and usage pattern. The Consignee should ensure that there should not be any financ ial loss to the ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Gulbarga. 13. Pharmacopoeia Specification IP/BP/USP etc. should be clearly mentioned against each drug/constituent of the formulation supplied as per the provisions of Drug and Cosmetics Act. 14. The items accepted should comply with the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder as amended upto date and Drug Price Control Order. 15. It should be ensured that ISI Code No. is indicated on the packing and at the time of supplies, it must be e nsured that the items supplied has ISI Mark as well as Code No.,as is the statutory requirement of the Bure au of Indian Standards (Where ever Applicable). 16. Testing of Drugs – Quality Control a. Approved Vendor should mandatorily submit a Test Report for that particular batch of medici nes tested by the Government/Government approved Laboratories along with each supply, failing which supply received will be liable for rejection at the inspection stage and penalty of l ate supply will be levied as per provisions. b. The Competent Authority shall be at liberty to undertake regular and random testing of the dr ugs supplied by the approved Vendors at regular interval to maintain and ensure the quality of drugs. c. Details of the items found not of standard quality should be brought to the notice of the Comp etent Authority along with the test reports immediately. A copy of the test report should be se

nt immediately to the firm, the concerned Drug controllers, and respective Central Drug Contro l authorities for necessary action. d. The report of the Govt./Govt. approved laboratory shall be accepted by the approved Vendor. In case the same is disputed by the approved Vendor the report of the Appellate Laboratory on ly will be accepted as final. However, the same should be submitted within three months, from the date of communication of the disputed test report to the approved Pharmaceutical firm. Fo r this, the approved Vendor should approach the concerned Drug Control Authorities for gettin g the drugs tested, as per procedure, from the Appellate Laboratory at their own cost. In case no response is received from the approved Vendor within the stipulated period, action as dee med fit as per terms & conditions of the contract will be initiated. e. For imported items: - The approved Vendor must submit the In-house test report of Principal manufacturer with each and every batch of supply. f. If any drug/s supplied against this contract are found to be "Not of Standard Quality" on inspe ction by Competent Authority, the approved Vendor will be liable to replace the entire quantity within 15 days otherwise risk purchase will be charged from the approved Vendor. g. If the product is found to be "Not of Standard Quality", the cost of testing will be recovered fro m the approved Vendor. 17. If any item/Batch of the item declared Not of Standard quality (NSQ), action may be taken against the ven dor including Recall of the NSQ item from ESIC Medical College and Hospital Gulbarga and Suitable forfeitu re of Performance Security. 18.
